title: The famous bitcoin pizza was an open offer, not a one off.
description:
The famous bitcoin pizza was an open offer, not a one off. Laszlo Hanyecz posted on a forum that he would pay 10,000 bitcoin for a couple of pizzas.

Programmer who bought two Papa John's pizzas on 22 May 2010, the first known commercial bitcoin transaction.

The price he paid for two pizzas. Nasdaq puts the pizzas at about 41 dollars at the time.

Someone else paid with their own money. Jeremy Sturdivant ordered the pizzas and received the 10,000 bitcoin in return.

He said he could not keep doing it. Hanyecz wrote that he could not generate thousands of coins a day any more.

The pizza was cheap. The offer was the story.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laszlo_Hanyecz - Wikipedia; established that on 22 May 2010 programmer Laszlo Hanyecz bought two Papa John's pizzas for 10,000 bitcoin, described as the first known commercial transaction using bitcoin.
- https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/happy-bitcoin-pizza-day - Nasdaq; established that Jeremy Sturdivant ordered the pizzas with his own money and received the 10,000 bitcoin, and that the pizzas were worth about $41 at the time.
- https://bitcointalk.org/index.php?topic=5453728.0 - Bitcointalk thread; quotes Hanyecz offering 10,000 BTC for a couple of pizzas, then keeping the offer open, later saying he could not afford to keep doing it because he could not generate thousands of coins a day any more. The claim that he bought eight pizzas for 40,000 bitcoin appears there only via tweets and is disputed in the replies.
